ov: A toothed whale of the Arctic waters of Canada, Greenland and Russia, closely related to the beluga; the two can interbreed. Males have a spiralled tusk 1.5–3 m long, an overgrown left canine tooth. It has no true dorsal fin, only a shallow ridge.

why.et: The Inuit have hunted narwhals for meat and ivory for thousands of years, and still do under regulation.

df: Mainly polar and Arctic cod, Greenland halibut, cuttlefish, shrimp and armhook squid.

cf.tip: Narwhals and belugas are close relatives, similarly built and known to interbreed; only the narwhal has a tusk.

fx: Narwhals spend long periods at great depths.
Narwhals usually travel in groups of three to eight, but in summer up to 1,000 gather together.
notes: The existing fact is mostly confirmed: the tusk is the left tooth with "millions of nerve endings". The article doesn’t say ten million. Suggested wording: "The tusk is an overgrown left tooth, packed with millions of nerve endings." No why.et: the source doesn’t mention it being eaten.
